chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:

I said to Zurara, 'I heard Muhammad ibn Muslim and Bukayr narrating from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a husband, two parents, and a daughter. So for the husband is a quarter, three shares from twelve, and for the two parents are two sixths, four shares from twelve, and five shares remain, so they are for the daughter, because if she were a male, she would not have other than five shares from twelve; and if there were two females, so for both of them is five shares from twelve, because if they were two males, they would not have other than what remains, five shares from twelve.'

Zurara said, 'This is the truth, when you want to apply the 'awl (deficiency/proportioning), so make the fixed shares such that they do not suffer 'awl. Indeed, the reduction enters only upon those who have the excess from the children and the sisters from the father and the mother. As for the husband and the brothers from the mother, indeed they are not reduced from what Allah has named for them.'

key_terms.الزِّيَادَة: Al-Ziyadah: The excess or surplus share that allows for the application of 'awl.
key_terms.النُّقْصَان: Al-Nuqsan: The reduction or deficiency applied to shares.
key_terms.عَوْل: Al-'awl: The method of proportioning shares when the sum of fixed heirs' portions exceeds the total estate.
key_terms.فَرِيضَة: Al-Faridah: The fixed, Quranically legislated shares of inheritance.

ai.seo_question: How is the 'awl (deficiency) applied in inheritance when fixed shares exceed the total estate?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'awl (proportioning), where Zurara affirms that in cases of excess shares, the reduction falls upon the 'asabah (residuary heirs) or those with variable shares, such as the daughter, rather than the fixed-share holders like the husband and parents. This contrasts with some Sunni schools by protecting the husband's quarter and the parents' sixth from being diminished below their Quranic quotas, ensuring the estate is distributed proportionally among the remaining heirs. The narration highlights the scholarly consensus on maintaining the integrity of specific Quranic portions while adjusting the residuary share to fit the total estate.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, altogether from Umar Bin Azina who said,

‘I said to Zurara, ‘I heard Muhammad Bin Muslim and Bukeyr both narrating form Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding a husband and two parents and a daughter. So for the husband would be a quarter, three shares from twelve, and for the two parents would be a sixth (each coming to), four shares from twelve, and the remaining five shares, so it is for the daughter, because had she been a male she would not have other than five shares from twelve; and if there were two females, so for the both of them would be five shares from twelve, because they both, had they been two males, would not have had other than what remains, five shares from twelve’.

Zurara said, ‘This is the truth, when you want to receive the deficiency, so make the Obligations (legislated shares) with no deficiencies. But rather, the deficiency is upon the one for whom is the excess – from the son, and the sisters from the father, and the mother. So, as for the husband and the brothers of the mother, so they would not be reduced from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Named something for them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from and Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman all from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah who has narrated the following: “I once said to Zurarah that I have heard Muhammad ibn Muslim and Bukayr narrating from abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the husband, both parents and a daughter. The share of the husband is one-fourth, three shares out of twelve shares, the parents receive two-sixth, four shares out of twelve shares and the remaining five shares belong to the daughter because if she were a male she would not have more than five out of twelve shares. If they were two daughters, they would have five out of twelve shares because if they were two males they would not have anything other than the five remaining from twelve shares.

Zurarah then said, ‘This is right. If you face deficiency, you must not place deficiency on ordained shares. Deficiency is placed on those who have extra, like children and sisters from the side of the father and mother. Husband and brothers from the side of mother do not pay the deficiency from the ordained shares that Allah has made for them.”’
